entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
This is successive bail petition filed by the sole accused to grant him bail in Crime No.306/2022 (Spl. S.C. POCSO 03/2023) for the offence punishable under Section 363, 343 and 376 of IPC read with Section 6 of Protection of Child from Sexual Offence Act, 2012 (for short "POCSO Act").
2. In support of his petition, the petitioner/accused has contended that there is no nexus between him and the alleged incident.

entities.text: Protection of Child from Sexual Offence Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: At the time of her evidence, the prosecutrix has not supported the prosecution case and she has given a clear go by to the entire case of the prosecution.

The statement of NC: 2023:KHC-D:13336 prosecutrix given under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., indicates that she has willfully joined the company of petitioner/accused and went to Hulagi Railway Station and to Hospet and thereafter, they went to a small village and stayed in factory for some time and led life with petitioner/accused.
In the light of the subsequent developments, no purpose would serve by keeping the petitioner/accused in custody.
He is ready and and willing to abide by any conditions imposed and offer substantial surety to the satisfaction of the trial Court and prays to allow the petition.

3. Learned High Court Government Pleader submitted oral objections stating that the mother of the prosecutrix by name Smt.Tulasi D/o Bhavani shankar, has filed the complaint on 25.11.2022, stating that the prosecutrix is her elder daughter.
Complainant is having two sons, aged about 12 and 3 years.
The prosecutrix is studying in 9th standard.
On 25.11.2022 at about 9.00 a.m. as usual prosecutrix is left the house to go to school NC: 2023:KHC-D:13336 at Hasalingapura.
She did not return home at 5.00 p.m. as usual and thinking that she may be with her friends complainant kept quiet.

After 6.00 p.m. when she did not return, complainant went in search of her and when she enquired her teacher telephonically, she told the complainant that the prosecutrix has not come to the School on that day.
After searching her everywhere, she lodged a missing complaint.
As on the day of complaint, prosecutrix was aged about 14 years 10 months.

3.1. Based on the complaint, case was registered in Crime No.306/2022 (SPl. S.C. POCSO Sri Manjunath S/O Hulugappa Lamani vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83238512/
2 No.03.2023) for the offence under Section 363 of IPC and investigation was taken up.

sentences.text: During investigation, the petitioner/accused and prosecutrix were secured from Chikkuru of Arsikere and the interrogation of the accused and enquiry with the prosecutrix, it was revealed that about 3 years prior to the date of complaint, she came in contact with the petitioner/accused.

On 11.10.2022, while she was speaking to the petitioner/accused at Hulagi Railway NC: 2023:KHC-D:13336 Station, her uncle Ramanjaneya saw her and informed her mother and she was advised by her mother.
3.2. On 24.11.2022 petitioner/accused told her that they would run away from the house.
Accordingly, on 25.11.2022, after telling her mother that she is going to the school prosecutrix went to Hulagi Bus stand.
From there along with the petitioner/accused, they went to Hospete and from Hospete in train they went to Chikuru of Arsikere.
They stayed in a black papper factory.
While staying in the room of the factory petitioner/accused had committed sexual intercourse with her against her consent.
On 01.12.2022, Police apprehended and brought them back.
3.3. Both petitioner/accused and prosecutrix were subjected to medical examination.
The medical report of the prosecutrix reveals that hymen is ruptured and possibility sexual intercourse cannot be ruled out.
After conducting detailed investigation, charge sheet is filed against the petitioner/accused which makes out a strong NC: 2023:KHC-D:13336 prima facie case.
Even now the prosecutrix is a minor.
The trial is going on.

The very fact that the prosecutrix has turned hostile,
goes to show that if released on bail the petitioner/accused may also tamper the other witnesses and prays to reject the petition.

4. Heard arguments and perused the records.
5.
From the material placed on record, it is evident that as on the date of complaint, prosecutrix was aged about 14 years 10 months.
She was studying in 9th standard.
On 25.11.2022, as usual she left the home to go to the school.
However, she did not return in the evening.

Her mother i.e.
complainant called her teacher.
Her teacher said that prosecutrix has not attended the school on that day.
Thereafter, she filed a missing complaint.
6. During investigation, the investigating officer has arrested the petitioner and found the prosecutrix in his company.
Both of them were subjected to medical examination, which reveals that prosecutrix is sexually assaulted by the petitioner/accused.

After conducting NC:
2023:KHC-D:13336 detailed investigation, charge sheet is filed against the petitioner/accused.
7. The trial Court has rejected bail petition filed by the petitioner/accused.
The earlier bail petition filed by the petitioner/accused was rejected by this Court on the ground that trial is yet to commence.
Now, the trial has progressed wherein the prosecutrix and some of the material witnesses are examined.
The deposition of the prosecutrix indicate that she has turned hostile and given a total go by to the case of the prosecution.
In the light of the same, this Court is of the considered opinion that the petitioner/accused is entitled for bail.

Of course the interest of the prosecution is required to be safeguarded by imposing stringent conditions and accordingly, the following:

sentences.text: ORDER Petition filed by the petitioner/accused under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. is allowed.

He is released on bail with the following:
NC: 2023:KHC-D:13336 CONDITIONS a) The petitioner/accused shall execute a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
with two sureties for the like-sum to the satisfaction of the trial Court.
b) The petitioner/accused shall not contact the prosecutrix.
c) The petitioner/accused shall make himself available for the purpose of investigation as and when required and he shall co-operate with the investigation.
d) The petitioner/accused shall furnish his residential address proof and shall inform the Investigating Officer/Court if there is any change in the address.
e) The petitioner/accused shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses either directly or indirectly.
f) The petitioner/accused shall not indulge in any criminal activities.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:13336 g) The petitioner/accused shall be regular in attending the Court proceedings.
